extracted.intended_audience: IRF providers and administrators, hospital finance officers, policy analysts, and stakeholders responding to or implementing the FY 2025 IRF PPS final rule
extracted.subtask_short: IRF PPS FY2025 RIA and policies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and analytic standards for updating inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF) prospective payment system (PPS) rates for FY 2025, including the regulatory impact analysis (RIA), payment- and quality-related policy changes, data collection/burden estimates, and distributional reporting requirements. Targeted at entities affected by or implementing the IRF PPS and IRF QRP changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory requirement to update IRF PPS rates and publish classification/weighting factors
rubrics_metrics.description: This final rule updates the IRF prospective payment rates for FY 2025 as required under section 1886(j)(3)(C) of the Act and in accordance with section 1886(j)(5) of the Act, which requires the Secretary to publish in the Federal Register on or before August 1 before each FY, the classification and weighting factors for CMGs used under the IRF PPS for such FY and a description of the methodology and data used in computing the prospective payment rates under the IRF PPS for that FY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish classification and weighting factors and a description of methodology/data in the Federal Register on or before Aug 1 each FY; updates must implement statutory directives cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Productivity adjustment to market basket percentage increase
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1886(j)(3)(C) of the Act requires the Secretary to apply a productivity adjustment to the market basket percentage increase for FY 2012 and subsequent years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For FY 2025 the IRF market basket percentage increase of 3.5 percent is reduced by a 0.5 percentage point productivity adjustment, yielding a 3.0 percent update (market basket less productivity adjustment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to adopt IRF QRP changes under statutory discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: This final rule adopts policy changes to the IRF QRP under the statutory discretion afforded to the Secretary under section 1886(j)(7) of the Act. This rule updates the IRF QRP requirements beginning with the FY 2028 IRF QRP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy changes to quality reporting (IRF QRP) may be finalized by the Secretary under section 1886(j)(7); specific timing (e.g., beginning FY2028) and collection requirements should be stated in preamble and OMB information collection requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Significant Regulatory Action' (EO 12866 as amended by EO 14094)
rubrics_metrics.description: The amended section 3(f) of Executive Order 12866 defines a “significant regulatory action” as an action that is likely to result in a rule: (1) having an annual effect on the economy of $200 million or more in any 1 year ...; (2) creating a serious inconsistency or otherwise interfering with an action taken or planned by another agency; (3) materially altering the budgetary impacts of entitlement grants, user fees, or loan programs or the rights and obligations of recipients thereof; or (4) raise legal or policy issues for which centralized review would meaningfully further the President's priorities ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition to determine whether OIRA centralized review and RIA preparation are required; the $200M threshold is adjusted over time by OIRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to prepare a Regulatory Impact Analysis (RIA) for major rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A regulatory impact analysis (RIA) must be prepared for major rules with significant regulatory action/s and/or with significant effects as per section 3(f)(1) ($200 million or more in any 1 year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a rule meets the EO 12866/14094 significant-action threshold, prepare an RIA that presents costs and benefits and follows applicable OMB guidance (e.g., Circular A-4). The FY2025 IRF PPS RIA compares FY2025 to FY2024 payments and estimates aggregate impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for estimating impacts in RIA (hold other variables constant; no behavioral adjustments)
rubrics_metrics.description: We estimate the total impact of the policy updates described in this final rule by comparing the estimated payments in FY 2025 with those in FY 2024. We determined the effects by estimating payments while holding all other payment variables constant. We use the best data available, but we do not attempt to predict behavioral responses to these changes, and we do not make adjustments for future changes in such variables as number of discharges or case-mix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact estimates are static (no behavioral response) and compare payment systems year-to-year holding other factors constant; note forecasting uncertainty and limitations in discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: RFA small entity impact thresholds and analysis approach
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS generally uses a revenue impact of 3 to 5 percent as a significance threshold under the Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA). The RFA requires agencies to analyze options for regulatory relief of small entities, if a rule has a significant impact on a substantial number of small entities. For purposes of the RFA, small entities include small businesses, nonprofit organizations, and small governmental jurisdictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing small-entity impacts, identify affected entities and estimate revenue/revenue-impact percentages; if impacts exceed 3–5% on a substantial number, analyze alternatives. In this analysis CMS assumes all IRFs (approx. 1,160) are small entities for conservatism when data on receipts are lacking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small rural hospital analysis requirement under section 1102(b) and RFA section 604
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1102(b) of the Act requires an RIA if a rule may have a significant impact on the operations of a substantial number of small rural hospitals. This analysis must conform to the provisions of section 604 of the RFA. For purposes of section 1102(b) of the Act, we define a small rural hospital as a hospital that is located outside of a Metropolitan Statistical Area and has fewer than 100 beds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide discrete analysis for small rural hospitals (definition: outside MSA and <100 beds), estimate percent impacts and whether they are significant, and conform to RFA sec. 604 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act (UMRA) assessment threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 202 of the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act of 1995 (UMRA) requires agencies to assess anticipated costs and benefits before issuing any rule whose mandates require spending in any 1 year of $100 million in 1995 dollars, updated annually for inflation. In 2024, that threshold is approximately $183 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether rule mandates impose costs above the UMRA threshold (adjusted dollars) and, if so, prepare required analyses; note this final rule does not mandate requirements for State/local/Tribal governments or the private sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 13132 federalism considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Order 13132 establishes certain requirements that an agency must meet when it issues a proposed rule (and subsequent final rule) that imposes substantial direct requirement costs on State and local governments, preempts State law, or otherwise has federalism implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and describe federalism implications; state whether the rule imposes direct costs on State/local governments, preempts State law, or has other federalism impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage index, labor-related share update and 5-percent cap on decreases
rubrics_metrics.description: We are applying the budget-neutral labor-related share and wage index adjustment, accounting for the permanent cap on wage index decreases when applicable. As discussed in section VI.E., we are updating the FY 2025 labor-related share from 74.1 percent in FY 2024 to 74.4 percent in FY 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying wage index/labor-related share updates, account for the 5% cap on decreases and apply changes budget-neutrally across providers; document impacts in reporting tables and narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update outlier threshold to target 3 percent of total payments
rubrics_metrics.description: We are adjusting the outlier threshold amount in this final rule to maintain total estimated outlier payments equal to 3 percent of total estimated payments in FY 2025. For the FY 2025 proposed rule ... estimated IRF outlier payments as a percentage of total estimated IRF payments would be 3.2 percent in FY 2024 ... adjusting the outlier threshold amount to maintain estimated outlier payments at 3 percent of estimated aggregate payments in FY 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set outlier threshold so outlier payments approximate statutory/target share (3%); quantify effect on total payments (here ~0.2 percentage point decrease).

rubrics_metrics.name: Update CBSA delineations and report distributional effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Present the effects of revised FY2025 CBSA delineations (without applying some rural adjustments for transitions) and report that in aggregate these updates do not affect overall estimated payments but do have small distributional effects across regions and provider types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both aggregate and distributional impacts of CBSA delineation changes; highlight largest increases/decreases by region and provider type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-year phase-out of rural adjustment for IRFs transitioning rural→urban
rubrics_metrics.description: To mitigate effects for IRFs transitioning from rural to urban status under new CBSA delineations, we will phase-out the rural adjustment for these providers over a 3-year period: two thirds of the rural adjustment in FY 2025, one third in FY 2026, and none in FY 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a budget-neutral phased implementation to soften payment shocks for transitioning providers; quantify percent payment reductions per year (e.g., two-thirds→one-third→none) and report distributional impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget-neutral updates to CMG relative weights and ALOS values
rubrics_metrics.description: We are updating the CMG relative weights and ALOS values under authority of section 1886(j)(2)(C)(i) of the Act and presenting these updates in a budget-neutral manner. In the aggregate, we do not estimate that these updates will affect overall estimated payments of IRFs, but we expect small distributional effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Update case-mix group weights and average lengths-of-stay to reflect recent data; apply budget-neutral scaling so aggregate payments remain constant while payment distribution may change (expected effects range -0.1 to 0.2 percent for some providers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents and column definitions for impact Table (Table 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table 17 shows the overall impact on the 1,160 IRFs included in the analysis. The next 12 rows contain IRFs categorized by geographic location, freestanding/unit, ownership, etc. The remaining five parts show grouping by urban/rural status before and after CBSA delineations, geographic region, teaching status, and DSH patient percentage. Columns: (1) facility classification categories; (2) number of IRFs in each category; (3) number of cases; (4) estimated effect of adjustment to outlier threshold; (5a) estimated effect of labor-related share and wage index (FY2024 CBA delineations) with 5% cap; (5b) similar with FY2025 CBSA delineations; (5c) effects of 3-year phase-out of rural adjustment; (6) effect of CMG/ALOS updates; (7) comparison of payments per discharge FY2025 vs FY2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting impact tables, include clear row/column definitions and separate columns for each policy component to allow readers to see distributional vs aggregate impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRF QRP penalty application (2 percentage point reduction)
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with section 1886(j)(7)(A) of the Act, the Secretary must reduce by 2 percentage points the annual market basket increase factor otherwise applicable to an IRF for a fiscal year if the IRF does not comply with the requirements of the IRF QRP for that fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe method for applying the 2-percentage-point reduction to noncompliant IRFs (discussed in section IX.A.); quantify implications for affected providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRF-PAI SDOH data collection changes and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalizing proposal to collect four new items as standardized patient assessment data elements under the SDOH category and modify one item collected as a standardized patient assessment data element under the SDOH category on the IRF-PAI beginning with the FY 2028 IRF QRP. Also finalizing removal of Item 14—Admission Class from the IRF-PAI effective October 1, 2026, with IRFs no longer required to collect and submit data on Item 14 beginning with patients admitted on October 1, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide OMB information collection updates (control number 0938-0842), state assumed completion roles/timing, and explicitly present burden and cost impacts by admission and per-IRF annual amounts (see Table 18 & Table 19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden estimation methodology for new/removed data elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate burden using assumed staff mix (items completed equally by RN 50% and LPN/LVN 50%), use BLS median hourly wages (May 2022) for those occupations, and double the hourly wage to account for indirect costs and fringe benefits. Example: estimated annual burden increase of 8,859.64 hours and $578,622.76 for all IRFs based on admissions and time-per-admission calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When calculating information-collection burden and costs, state staff time assumptions (who completes items), cite BLS wage sources, account for indirect/fringe by doubling wage, and present both aggregate and per-IRF burden and cost impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumptions and methods for regulatory review cost estimation
rubrics_metrics.description: If regulations impose administrative costs on private entities, estimate regulatory review cost. CMS assumes number of unique commenters on the proposed rule equals number of reviewers of this final rule, that each reviewer reads approximately 50 percent of the rule, and that it will take approximately 3 hours for staff to review half of this final rule. Using May 2023 BLS national mean hourly wage for medical and health service managers ($129.28/hr) including indirect costs, estimated cost per reviewer is $387.84 and total reviewing cost $17,064.96 (44 reviewers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State assumptions (reviewers = commenters; percent of rule read; review time per person) and wage basis; present per-reviewer and total review cost estimates and caveats about possible over/underestimation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare an Accounting Statement per OMB Circular A-4
rubrics_metrics.description: As required by OMB Circular A-4, prepare an accounting statement showing the classification of the expenditures associated with the provisions of this final rule. Table 20 provides estimates of the increase in Medicare payments ($280 million), estimated FY2028 IRF QRP data collection costs ($392,113.40), and estimated regulatory review costs ($17,064.96).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow OMB Circular A-4 in classifying transfers, costs, and monetized impacts; present annualized monetized transfers and costs and identify 'from whom to whom' for transfers.
